name: Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
role: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (2025-); environmental lawyer; 2024 independent presidential candidate
summary: Environmental litigator turned vaccine-skeptic activist who ran for president in 2023-24 as a Democrat, then independent, before endorsing Donald Trump and becoming HHS secretary. He combines hostility to corporate capture of regulators and to foreign wars and censorship with support for stricter food and chemical rules and tougher border enforcement. His stances on abortion, healthcare and guns have shifted or been hedged.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Told reporters in 2023 his 'highest ambition' would be a single program available to everyone, with private plans allowed, while calling it politically unrealistic. As HHS secretary in 2026 he says the answer is not single-payer or Obamacare but paying the consumer directly and making them 'CEO' of their own care, and he did not commit to guaranteeing coverage at his hearing. Mixed record.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says he has 'great admiration and love' for capitalism as 'the greatest economic engine ever devised' but insists it be 'harnessed to a social purpose' and policed by regulators; called himself a 'free-market absolutist' on energy generation (no subsidies, costs internalized).

unions-good.rationale: Lists 'protection of labor, dignity, and decent pay for labor' among his core values and says he worked closely with Cesar Chavez in the last decade of Chavez's life. No statement on unions as such.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Decades of suits against polluters; says corporations are 'poisoning our children'; calls for a regulatory structure free of industry capture; campaign page promises to end 'corporate capture' and ban food additives other countries prohibit; as secretary changed food and dietary rules.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Sued industrial factory farms on behalf of independent family farmers; campaign proposed policies favoring small and medium businesses over concentrated corporate power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Campaign proposed to break up 'too-big-to-fail' banks and monopolies and favor small and medium businesses.

no-bailouts.rationale: Campaign line: when crisis strikes 'bail out the homeowners, debtors, and small business owners instead' of banks.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Told The Hill in 2023 he supports 'some kind of massive debt forgiveness' for student loans.

corporate-influence.rationale: Names the 'corrupt merger of state and corporate power' as the main threat to democracy; says half of FDA's budget comes from pharma and that regulatory capture is 'on steroids'; campaign page promises to 'end the era of corporate capture'.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Campaign and interviews attack the merger of state and corporate power and regulatory capture, which amounts to opposing special legal treatment for connected firms.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Says 'huge aggregations of wealth above and widespread poverty below' is 'too unstable to support democracy sustainably' and warns of a 'Latin American style' oligarchy.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Names protection of the most vulnerable and restoration of the middle class as core values and praises his uncle for putting America 'on the side of the poor'.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wants capitalism combined with a social purpose and a regulatory regime, otherwise it leads to oligarchy, environmental destruction and poisoning of consumers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Campaign page lists surveillance, censorship and propaganda as assaults on constitutional rights; campaign emails defended Snowden as wrongly stripped of liberties. No statement on the terrorism trade-off specifically.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Campaign page says freedom of speech must be protected and calls censorship an assault on rights; he has not discussed hate-speech laws specifically.

state-harmful.rationale: Argues government must regulate drugs, food and pollution and run health programs; served as HHS secretary. Criticizes capture and corruption, not the state's existence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Calls for a 'solid regulatory regimen' for drugs, environmental protection of the commons, and acts as a cabinet secretary running health programs, which goes well beyond defense, justice and property.

limit-guns.rationale: Campaign page lists the right to bear arms among Constitutional rights to protect; says he will not take guns away and that the Second Amendment question was settled by the Supreme Court, though he said he'd sign an assault weapons ban if Congress passed one.

party-controls-media.rationale: Campaign page says freedom of the press must be protected and calls government control of media and propaganda an assault on rights; accuses government and media of collusion to censor.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Campaign page defends free speech and assembly against government censorship and says Democratic elites now police speech.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Reported to have long supported legalizing gay marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: 2023: told Reuters abortion is a tragedy but a right throughout pregnancy; a remark at the Iowa State Fair about a ban after three months was disavowed by his campaign. At his 2025 hearing he said he would implement Trump's policy, shares the view that every abortion is a tragedy, and that Trump wants to end late-term abortion. Latest clear stance is deference, so earlier support for legality is recorded at low confidence.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Said transgender people deserve respect and that he supports people's 'gender choices' while opposing transgender women in women's sports.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Writes that God speaks through wise people, religion, art and creation, and that destroying nature diminishes our capacity to sense the divine; describes modern life as a 'spiritual malaise'.

minority-language-support.rationale: Criticizes Ukraine's ban on Russian language in public life and says the Minsk accords let the Donbas keep its language.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Describes the Minsk accords' semi-autonomous status for Russian-speaking Donbas as a sound settlement the US sabotaged.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Supports enforcement and deportation of illegal immigrants and says mass illegal immigration strains health care, housing and jobs, but also says legal immigrants are needed.

open-borders.rationale: Says Democrats' 'open borders' were a mistake, that the border was wide open for four years, and calls for stronger enforcement and a wall; supports Texas's border stance.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Says 'exemplary nation' rhetoric was turned by neocons into justification for forcing systems at gunpoint; criticizes humanitarian framing of Ukraine war; campaign page opposes regime-change wars.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Campaign page promises to abstain from military interventions and regime-change wars; urges ending proxy wars and forever wars.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said the US must 'start unraveling the Empire' by closing bases abroad and criticizes NATO expansion; did not call for ending alliances outright.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Wants to 'end the proxy wars, bombing campaigns, covert operations, coups, paramilitaries'; criticizes using Ukraine and Afghanistan as proxy wars.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposes regime-change wars, covert operations and coups and says Russia's security concerns were ignored; does not frame it as an absolute ban on any intervention.

national-mission.rationale: Says America should be an example of democracy, not impose it by force; rejects the neocon use of 'exemplary nation'.

arms-reduction.rationale: Wants verifiable arms reduction treaties with China and Russia and treaties on AI and bioweapons; says military spending ruined the budget.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called Israel a 'moral nation' justly responding to Hamas and opposed a Gaza ceasefire in 2024; no statement specifically on the right to a state.

close-ties-china.rationale: 2024: wanted competition on economic terms without decoupling. As secretary in 2025-26 he calls reliance on China for medicines and glyphosate a national security vulnerability to be brought home. Recent position wins.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Praises Alliance for Progress and USAID aid to the poorest and says the US should return to that approach.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Campaign promises to unravel the web of secrecy and cover-ups; at his hearing stressed publishing raw data and openness; pushes hospital price transparency.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says Washington is captured by corporations and promises to 'get corruption out of Washington' and 'drain the swamp'.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Campaign slogan: 'Left isn't better. Right isn't better. Better is better.'

results-over-ideology.rationale: Campaign framing that policies should be judged by whether they are better, not by left or right, and he later joined Trump's cabinet citing shared goals.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Career in suing polluters on behalf of injured landowners, towns and tribes (Riverkeeper, Pace clinic, Kennedy & Madonna).

pollution-taxes.rationale: Told Elon Musk that companies should internalize costs 'including the cost of pollution' with no subsidies.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Campaign and HHS record: ban additives and chemicals other countries have prohibited; letter on acetaminophen in pregnancy acted on association evidence rather than certainty.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Wrote a climate book and litigated for decades, but in 2024 vowed to repeal parts of the Inflation Reduction Act's climate subsidies and favors unsubsidized markets.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Led a 34-year campaign that closed Indian Point; Wikipedia reports he opposes nuclear as clean energy; limited, secondhand.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Says the commons (air, water, wildlife, public lands) cannot be reduced to private property and that nature is a path to the divine.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Calls AI and biological weapons existential threats needing treaties and regulation, and nuclear confrontation with Russia the major danger.

notes: Views moved from environmental Democrat to 2024 independent to Trump cabinet member. Where 2023-24 campaign statements conflict with his 2025-26 record (abortion, healthcare, China), the later position was used where clear. Many topics (taxes, welfare, courts, social issues) have no recorded position in the sources read and are left null. Abortion and Israel answers rest partly on secondhand reporting of his remarks.
